clue.text: It's bound to attract the wealthier reader

definitions.text: It's bound to attract the wealthier reader

blocks.clueFragment: It's bound to attract the wealthier reader
blocks.note: surface reading: something certain to appeal to a well-off person
setter's reading: bound as in a book's binding, a lavish volume priced for richer buyers

explanation.surface: Something sure to win over a well-heeled customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but it means bound in covers, as a book is.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluxe edition is a luxurious, expensively produced printing of a book aimed at collectors with money to spend.

clue.text: Snaps come out and go round

indicators.note: letters that come out are freed from their original order and can fall into a new one

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Photographs are developed and passed around the room.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass something is to surround or encircle it, which is a verb sense of going round it.

blocks.note: first meaning: oneness, the number one or a state of being one
second meaning: ... Mitford, one of the six famous Mitford sisters

explanation.walkthrough: The Mitfords were six aristocratic English sisters of the 1920s-40s, among them Nancy, Jessica and Unity. 'One' reads as part of the phrase but is a definition of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity is the mathematical term for the number one and also means wholeness; it was also the first name of a Mitford sister.

clue.text: Cheer a team endlessly at finale

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the team word is dropped

blocks.note: a cricket or football side has eleven players
taken as written
the finale of the word finale itself, its closing letter

explanation.surface: Fans rouse their side as the match nears its end.
explanation.walkthrough: A football or cricket team is an eleven; 'endlessly' trims its ending, and the finale of the clue word 'finale' supplies the closing letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate someone's spirits is to lift or raise them, so it can mean to cheer or hearten.

indicators.note: a translation renders a text in a new form, so these letters are rendered in a new order

blocks.note: de is French for of
taken as written

explanation.surface: Praising the quality of a rendering of French poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to be worthy of it, which is the verb sense of to merit.

clue.text: Advocates getting in money to create large food store

indicators.note: the lawyers get inside the money word, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the Bar is the collective term for barristers
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: Lawyers raking in cash to build a big granary.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is old British slang for money, and 'the Bar' is the whole body of barristers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn was a large medieval barn built to hold the produce paid to the church as tithes.

clue.text: Give an address or a note

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Deliver a speech or just pass on a short message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like a link offering two choices, but it supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, and an address is a formal speech to an audience.

clue.text: Speedy help appreciated by a forgetful actor?

blocks.note: first meaning: quick, efficient attention to customers
second meaning: the prompter's help from the wings to a performer who has dried

explanation.walkthrough: In theatre the prompter feeds lines to an actor who forgets them; the second reading takes 'prompt' in that stage sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt service is ordinary praise for quick help, and in a theatre it is the cueing done from the prompt corner.

clue.text: One may be orally examined in it

definitions.text: One may be orally examined in it

blocks.note: surface reading: given a viva, a spoken test, as a student might be

blocks.clueFragment: One may be orally examined in it
blocks.note: setter's reading: a seat where a patient has their mouth inspected

explanation.surface: Somewhere a candidate sits a spoken exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orally examined' suggests a viva voce exam; read literally it is having one's mouth looked at.
explanation.definitionFit: The reclining seat at a surgery is where a patient's teeth and mouth are inspected by a dental practitioner.

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the people who do this

blocks.note: first meaning: people who handle stolen goods
second meaning: officials appointed to manage bankrupt firms

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like crooks running failing firms; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Receivers handle stolen property, a crime, and official receivers are appointed to administer companies that cannot pay debts.

blocks.note: first meaning: to taunt or provoke
second meaning: to pester

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a lure set for the animal; 'badger' is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease is to provoke playfully or annoy persistently, matching both verbs as synonyms.

blocks.note: first meaning: an embalmed body, as in ancient Egypt
second meaning: a mother, in British usage

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a compliment to a youthful-looking parent. 'Mummy' is the usual British spelling of 'mommy'.
explanation.definitionFit: An embalmed Egyptian corpse is the ultimate preserved body, and the word is also a child's name for a mother.

blocks.note: first meaning: a formal pact or treaty
second meaning: a match or concurrence between things

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like 'brief letters'; 'Compact' is the noun meaning a pact, and 'correspondence' means things matching up.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreement is a pact between parties, and also the state of things being in accord, as in grammatical agreement.

indicators.note: when letters are ordered they are put into an arrangement different from the one given

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Buccaneers commanded on a gruelling march, perhaps along the plank.
explanation.definitionFit: A traipse is a tiring, trudging walk of some distance, used as a noun as well as a verb.

clue.text: Woman in service spoils ties in the press

indicators.note: to spoil something is to mess it up, so these letters are messed into a new order
one set of letters is placed inside the newspaper word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A female servant who wrecks neckties while ironing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' is a religious one, not domestic work, despite the ironing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A priestess is a female cleric who conducts rites at a religious service.

blocks.note: surface reading: the familiar exclamation at how quickly time goes
setter's reading: the verb for what time literally does as it passes

explanation.surface: The rueful remark that the years have slipped away.
explanation.definitionFit: When a period of time passes by, it is said to go by, slip away or run out, the verb used for time's passage.

blocks.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Remain behind for a round, then another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' is the noun, a prop or support, not 'remain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a brace or prop that holds something up, which is what a supporter does.

clue.text: Following points go to the prosecution

blocks.note: E and N, two compass points
suing is taking someone to court

explanation.surface: Next, a case is handed over to the prosecutors.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensuing means coming after or resulting from something, an adjective synonym for following.

definitions.note: the answer is past tense, complained

blocks.note: the middle of the word night is its centre letter
roused means woken up

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles at being woken in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places ROUSED after the G from the middle of 'night'.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to grumble or moan, an informal British synonym for complain.

blocks.note: can means is able
an opus is a work, especially of music

explanation.surface: A performer fit to get on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Canopus is the second-brightest star in the night sky, in the constellation Carina.

blocks.note: surface reading: a superb rider
setter's reading: belonging to fable, a mythical creature that is part man, part horse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means 'of legend', and the horseman is half horse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this creature has a human head and torso on a horse's body, literally a horse-man.

blocks.note: surface reading: strikes through with a pen
setter's reading: crosses on ballot papers rejecting a motion

explanation.walkthrough: A cross is the mark made on a ballot paper, so crosses can throw a proposal out.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject a proposal in a ballot is to defeat it by the number of crosses cast against it.

blocks.note: first meaning: a line of work, a craft or occupation
second meaning: swapping or bartering goods

explanation.walkthrough: 'Employment exchange' was the old British name for a job centre; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a skilled occupation, and to trade is to swap one thing for another in barter.

clue.text: He tangles with cop - that will mean time

indicators.note: tangled things are twisted together and jumbled out of their neat order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who scuffles with a policeman will be doing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' plays on a prison sentence; it is a period of history.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a distinct period or era, one of the senses of time as in 'in Victorian times'.

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters are not to be taken in their true order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit and set of guiding values of a group or culture.

clue.text: Finish with conclusion of judge in lawsuit

indicators.note: a conclusion is an ending, so only the final letter of the next word counts
the single letter is set inside the legal word

blocks.note: a case is a lawsuit
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A court action wraps up with the judge's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish with' looks like the definition plus a link; only 'Finish' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to stop or come to an end, a verb synonym for finish.

clue.text: Kind of Western food that's long in the cooking

definitions.text: food that's long in the cooking

blocks.note: first meaning: the Italian-made cowboy films of the 1960s

blocks.clueFragment: food that's long in the cooking
blocks.note: second meaning: long thin strands of pasta

explanation.walkthrough: 'Long in the cooking' suggests slow to cook; it means the food itself is long.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian-made cowboy films were nicknamed after pasta, and this pasta is made in long thin rods.

blocks.note: first meaning: a coastal resort sits by the sea, the main being the open sea
second meaning: a place people go for vacations

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the sea, not a main road. A seaside resort is a British coastal holiday town such as Blackpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal towns where tourists spend vacations by the beach are resorts beside the sea, near the main.
